slides.heading: Indexing Lists
slides.body: Indexing Lists is part of Lists and Mutable Sequences. This short lesson gives you a practical Python idea you can understand, try, and reuse in simple programs.

slides.heading: Core Idea: Indexing Lists
slides.body: List indexing gets one item from a list using its position. Python starts counting at index 0.

slides.heading: Real-World Analogy
slides.body: Indexing is like seat numbering that starts from 0 instead of 1 in Python's classroom.

slides.heading: Key Rule
slides.body: Lists use square brackets, zero-based indexes, and can be changed after creation.

slides.heading: Try It Yourself!
slides.prompt: Print the first item from a list named names.
slides.hint: Use names[0] to access the first item.

coding_challenge.prompt_text: Print the second item from animals = ["cat", "dog", "bird"].
coding_challenge.hint_text: Use the idea from the lesson. Keep the code short, readable, and correctly indented.
